convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iATR indicator and standard price data functions (CopyHigh, CopyLow, CopyClose). Simple channel breakout entry/exit rules. Fixed or risk-based position sizing with straightforward loss-reduction logic. No custom indicators or external trading logic libraries.

derived_values.name: Resist (Current channel high)
derived_values.formula: Maximum of CopyHigh over rChannel bars starting at bar 1

derived_values.name: ResistPrev (Previous channel high)
derived_values.formula: Maximum of CopyHigh over rChannel bars starting at bar 2

derived_values.name: Support (Current channel low)
derived_values.formula: Minimum of CopyLow over rChannel bars starting at bar 1

derived_values.name: SupportPrev (Previous channel low)
derived_values.formula: Minimum of CopyLow over rChannel bars starting at bar 2

other_exits: Buy position closed when channel high touched (hp1[0] >= Resist && Resist==ResistPrev) - same condition as open buy, acts as breakout exhaustion close
Sell position closed when channel low touched (lp1[0] <= Support && Support==SupportPrev) - same condition as open sell, acts as breakout exhaustion close

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If Lots != 0, use fixed Lots value. If Lots == 0, calculate from free margin fraction (MaxR). Then if DcF > 0, reduce lot size based on consecutive losing deals in history: aLots = aLots - aLots * losses / DcF

custom_logic_notes: Entry signals require channel stability (Resist==ResistPrev for buy, Support==SupportPrev for sell) meaning the channel boundary must not have shifted. Buy has two sub-conditions OR'd: (1) bar high touches/penetrates resistance with stable channel, or (2) close is between resistance and pivot with stable channel. Sell mirrors this with support. Close signals use the same channel-touch condition as open (buy closes when price touches resistance again, sell closes when price touches support again). Stop loss for sell adds the spread (Ask-Bid) to the ATR offset. The trailing stop only moves SL in profitable direction (buy: nsl >= open price; sell: nsl <= open price) and respects the broker's StopsLevel.
python_conversion_notes: Price channel logic must be reimplemented manually (rolling max of highs / min of lows over rChannel period). ATR is standard. The channel stability check (Resist==ResistPrev) after NormalizeDouble is essentially checking if the channel upper boundary remained the same when the window shifts by one bar - this is a float equality check on normalized prices that should translate safely. Lot reduction logic iterates deal history backwards counting consecutive losses - must replicate this exactly. The trailing stop implementation is standard but includes StopsLevel respect which requires broker parameter data. Entry uses previous completed bar data (shift 1+), so no lookahead bias. Position gate ensures only one position at a time per symbol.
